extra.WP-34:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 7 from WP-02] An *Object with more than 8 members keeps a name index that Decode, Clone and every mutation maintain. Decode charges CostIndexEntry (48) per member for that index, so for large objects the *Object form costs more than Options.MapObjects (map[string]any); budgets and reservations must use the cost Decode returns for the form you actually build. Reads (Len, At, All, Index, Get, Has) never write, so one decoded tree may be shared read-only by any number of goroutines (the shared decoded body of 03 req 25 and 07 req 56). Any mutation (Set, SetAt, Delete, DeleteAt, Sort, transforms, merge) needs exclusive access, so call Clone (jsonval.Clone or Object.Clone) before editing a shared tree. MaxCostPerByte (33) bounds cost per input byte; the oversize budget multiple is the one recorded in 2.16 for request 5 (4 times the raw limit).
- [CR 42 from WP-08] In internal/cel's Check, after type-checking, walk the checked AST (celast.PreOrderVisit over checked.NativeRep().Expr()). Report RZ-CFG-014 for every node where e.Kind() == celast.StructKind and celtypes.IsObjectType(e.AsStruct().TypeName()) is true, for example `ruralz.Error{kind: "connect"}`, `.ruralz.Error{}` and `[ruralz.Upstream{name: "a"}]`. Such a Bundle then fails at configuration time, instead of failing every evaluation with celtypes.ErrUnsupported and the place's runtime rule (such as 500 RZ-RT-006). Well-known types (`google.protobuf.Duration{seconds: 1}`) and type comparisons (`type(request) == ruralz.Request`) stay legal. TestIsObjectType in internal/cel/celtypes/eval_test.go shows the walk and the cases. Keep the celtypes runtime guard in Provider.NewValue as defense in depth.
- [CR 43 from WP-08] A missing map key, whether constant or computed (`request.headers[request.method]`), fails inside cel-go's attribute qualifier with the text 'no such key: <key>', not through celtypes.ErrNoSuchKey, and the key can be request data. internal/cel must classify runtime errors by kind (no such key, null, type, cost limit, interrupt) and build its own messages. It must never copy cel-go error text into EvalError.Error(), problem documents, logs or span events; only Detail may carry it (03 test 10). Add a 03 test 10 case with a computed key that holds a canary value (WP-34). In WP-91's runtime-error matrix, assert that the canary is absent from responses and logs.
- [Review note from WP-08, wave 2] cel-go v0.32.0 still hands an evaluation one shared *types.Err. types.NoSuchOverloadErr() returns the package-level celErrNoSuchOverload (common/types/err.go:89). Under cel.OptOptimize, Program adds interpreter.MatchesRegexOptimization for a constant pattern (cel/program.go:291-311), and its call returns that singleton when the receiver is not a string (interpreter/optimizations.go:37,41); String.Receive and Duration.Receive return it too. The interpreter's types.LabelErrNode writes the node ID into that shared value. A client can reach this: with body {"a":1}, `request.body.a.matches("^x")` type-checks because the body is dyn. Two Programs evaluating it concurrently race in LabelErrNode (go test -race reports it), and after the first label every later no-such-overload error reports a stale node ID. celtypes cannot fix this, because the error never passes through it. In internal/cel: (1) never use *types.Err.NodeID() to locate a no-such-overload error; classify it by kind (CR 43) and report no node or find the node another way. (2) Keep the shared value off the matches path. Either plan without the regex precompilation OptOptimize adds, or register a replacement through cel.OptimizeRegex whose non-string branch returns a fresh types.NewErr; check that it takes precedence, because decRegexOptimizer looks up overload IDs before function names and later entries win. (3) Add a -race test that evaluates such a Program from two goroutines. (4) Consider reporting the singleton to cel-go upstream.

Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 85 from WP-16] Lead decision: the tlsconf row of 1.2 stays 'secret, errcode' (no v1alpha1), so the v1alpha1-typed signatures that spec 06 section 3 sketches are not built. Listener certificates become `[]tlsconf.CertSpec{Name, Certificate: secret.RefOf(c.Certificate), PrivateKey: secret.RefOf(c.PrivateKey)}` for `tlsconf.BuildCertIndex(specs, store)`, then `tlsconf.NewListenerState(tlsconf.ListenerOptions{MinVersion, Certs, RequestClientCert})`; the snapshot compiler does this conversion. Upstream.spec.tls and telemetry.otlp.tls become `tlsconf.ClientSpec{SNI, CACertificate, ClientCertificate, ClientKey *secret.Ref}` for `tlsconf.Upstream(spec, store)` and `tlsconf.OTLP(&spec, store)` (nil spec: system roots). The owner calls Close on the CertIndex or ClientConfig when it retires it, which stops its secret watches.
- [CR 46 from WP-09] aggregate.Registry.Producer() returns *aggregate.Producer, an sdkmetric.Producer that pools its collection structures (09 req 51). Release points: (1) the Ruralz wrapper around the OTLP metric exporter calls Producer.ReleaseResource(rm) on the *metricdata.ResourceMetrics once its inner Export returns; (2) the /metrics handler wraps the Producer it passes to prometheus.WithProducer, records the []metricdata.ScopeMetrics that each Produce call returns during one Gather, and calls Producer.Release on each one after Gather and encoding finish. Release each result at most once. Data that is never released is abandoned after 30 s, which is safe but loses pooling. Test both release points: heap must not grow over repeated scrapes and exports.
- [CR 60 from WP-11] emit.NodeMetrics has no handles for ruralz_telemetry_logs_total{stream} or ruralz_telemetry_logs_dropped_total{stream,reason}, so read logsink.Sink.Stats() and accesslog.Writer.Stats() (Produced, QueueFull, ExportError). aggregate.Registry.GaugeFunc refuses counter families (registry_test 'func on counter'). Instead, get counter handles with Registry.Counter(catalog.TelemetryLogsTotal, stream) and Registry.Counter(catalog.TelemetryLogsDroppedTotal, stream, "queue_full"|"export_error"), with label values in catalog order. Before each collection, add the Stats deltas since the last sync. A good place is the Producer wrapper that WP-40 registers on the PeriodicReader and the Prometheus exporter; serialize the sync and keep the last totals. No emit change is needed. If this proves awkward, ask the lead for an additive aggregate.Registry.CounterFunc instead.
- [CR 61 from WP-11] Use one logsink.Sink per process: logsink.New with Options.Access set to the accesslog.Writer and Options.TraceContext reading the tracing span context. Sink.Run is the only stdout goroutine and runs on a goroutine the supervisor owns (WP-76). After each snapshot swap, call Sink.SetRevision(display) and Sink.SetCredentialHeaders(that Revision's auth.api-key header names), for example from Runtime.Apply, which WP-73 calls after publish. Implement logsink.Bridge over otelslog and accesslog.Bridge (event.name = accesslog.EventName, timestamp = record Start, observed timestamp = Observed), installed when an OTLP endpoint is configured. The Exported.Dropped flag keeps each record counted as dropped at most once (09 req 65). At Drain (Runtime.Shutdown), cancel Run's context, wait up to 5 s, then call Close on both the Sink and the Writer.
- [CR 108 from WP-21] The handler takes one stripe per connection from retire.Holder.ConnStripe, offset per request with Holder.RequestStripe(conn, streamID), and uses it for both Holder.Pin and every metric handle. It never calls emit.Meter.NewStripe itself. WP-76 computes the stripe count S once with retire.StripeCount() (min(GOMAXPROCS at start, 8)). It passes S as retire.Config.Stripes and, through WP-40's Runtime options, as the aggregate registry's stripe count (aggregate Config.Stripes; its default 0 means the same value). It also sets retire.Config.NewStripe = meter.NewStripe, so pins and metrics share one round robin (04 req 50). WP-40 accepts or exposes that stripe count so both sides agree.
- [CR 54 from WP-10] WP-40: build the tracer with tracing.New(tracing.Options{...}). Pass Clock, the shared Resource (the same *resource.Resource the meter and logger providers use; never resource.Default()) and OnExport. Fill Counters from the aggregate registry. Spans comes from aggregate.Registry.Counter(catalog.TelemetrySpansTotal). DroppedQueueFull and DroppedExportError come from Counter(catalog.TelemetrySpansDroppedTotal, "queue_full" or "export_error"). UnsampledRoot and UnsampledParent come from Counter(catalog.TelemetryTracesUnsampledTotal, "rate_cap_root" or "rate_cap_parent"). On Apply, install or swap the OTLP span exporter with Tracer.SetExporter. nil stops span creation while decisions and propagation continue, and the returned previous exporter is the Runtime's to shut down, off the request path and within its 5 s bound (spec 09 req 24). At Drain, call Tracer.Shutdown(ctx) with the 5 s flush deadline (req 25).

- [CR 3 from WP-15] Build each attempt's header to meet clientaddr.Rewrite's documented preconditions (internal/clientaddr/rewrite.go). Per attempt, start from a fresh clone of the leg's client header, using http.Header{} when it is nil: http.Header(nil).Clone() returns nil, and Rewrite panics with 'clientaddr: Rewrite called with a nil http.Header'. Next, remove hop-by-hop fields with httpfield.StripHopByHop(h, httpfield.TowardUpstream); the handler already ran StripConnectionOptions at admission. Then call clientaddr.Rewrite(h, f) exactly once, and only after that add the Node's own fields (traceparent). Never reuse a rewritten header for a retry, because with a trusted peer a second Rewrite appends the peer to X-Forwarded-For again. Add a retry test asserting one peer entry per attempt.
- [CR 102 from WP-18] At outgoing request build, call httpfield.StripHopByHop(h, httpfield.TowardUpstream), then add the forwarding headers (clientaddr) and traceparent (Tracer.Inject) after the strip. On every Upstream response, call httpfield.StripHopByHop(h, httpfield.TowardClient) before LegRun.OnUpstreamResponseHeaders and the response Phases, so an Upstream's Connection field cannot remove fields a response Policy sets. Composition steps use the same attempt loop, so this covers them. Always pass an explicit Direction: the zero value drops both Expect and TE (internal/httpfield/hopbyhop.go).
- [CR 114 from WP-22] This describes the balance API as committed; balance/doc.go is the reference, and it supersedes the Picker-interface proposal in spec 05 section 3. Construction: New(Config{Algorithm, VirtualNodes, Fallback, Endpoints in Normalize form, Payload, Rand, Now}) returns (*Balancer, error). Balancer methods: SetEndpoints(eps, payload), SetPlan(v, fallback), Load() *Set, RebuildDue(now), NextRebuild(), Rebuild(ctx, *BuildGate, now) (driven by the manager's scheduler with NewBuildGate(8)), and Info() for /debug/upstreams. Per attempt, load one Set and build the View from Set.Payload() (the per-Endpoint state published with that list), so View indexes and Choice.Index refer to the same list. Then call Set.Select(HashKey(key), src, view), or Set.SelectRandom(src, view) when hashKey fails; there is no Balancer.Select. View has Grade(i) Grade (use GradeOf(down, avoid)) and Load(i) int64 (LoadCounter.Score(now) or the runtime's own count); Choice has Index, Grade, Panic() and Relaxed(); ErrNoEndpoints maps to 503 RZ-UP-008. Budget side: PlanBudget/Replan(prev, budget, schedules, rings map[name]count), Plan.VirtualNodes(name), Plan.Warnings() (configuration warnings, OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-23 (b)) and Plan.Degraded() (balancer_budget), plus ScheduleBytes and RingBytes for sizing. Also exported: NewSplit/Split.Pick, EndpointCap and HashKey.

Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 125 from WP-26] WP-85: build statestoretest.FaultProxy and CountingProxy (spec 08's names) on internal/testkit/faultproxy instead of a second TCP proxy. Put them in internal/statestore/statestoretest/respproxy (architecture 1.2 and WP-85 scope): the statestoretest root may import only statestore and clock. Use faultproxy.Config.ConnTap for per-connection RESP command parsing (it returns each connection's own TapFunc, so parser state stays per connection) and Config.Tap for stateless counting. Proxy.SetConnMode and Proxy.Conns give the per-connection rules spec 08 asks for, and Proxy.SetUpstream gives scripted failover. A switch between Delay distributions, directly or through Pass or Blackhole, applies the new distribution at once.
- [CR 130 from WP-26] proc.Process.WaitOutput (internal/testkit/proc/proc.go:289-298) matches per line. The pattern is applied to each stdout and stderr line on its own, newline included, and to the growing unterminated last line, so a match never spans lines. Write single-line patterns (use (?m) for ^ and $ anchors) and never expect a multi-line match. Lines longer than proc.MaxLineBytes (64 KiB) are matched in pieces, so for long JSON log lines wait on a short, distinctive fragment rather than a pattern that could straddle a split. A capture can also come from a line still being written, because the unterminated last line is matched as it grows: end any pattern that captures a value from a complete line with `\n` (for example `listening on (\S+)\n`), since `$`, even under (?m), also matches at the end of a partial line.

- [CR 144 from WP-28] The rendered schema's $defs/JSONSchemaDocument (validation.json-schema config.schema: type [object, boolean], no properties) is opaque. Detect it through schemaidx: its Node has Def() == "JSONSchemaDocument" (Def follows the $ref), and every position below it is Info.Free with a nil Node. WP-36 overlay: an overlay value at that node replaces the base value whole and never merges recursively (docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md Overlays table, 'Replaced whole as one atomic value'; 07 req 74). WP-36 subst: string scalars inside are substituted like any other free string (a literal ${ is written $${) and are never re-typed. WP-37: normalize its object keys generically (02 req 18), materialize no defaults inside it, and keep every list inside in authored order (schemaidx ListNone is atomic, 02 req 17). Add tests: an overlay that changes one keyword replaces the whole document, and normalization keeps the order of `enum` and `required`.
- [CR 19 from WP-04] WP-37 (stage G defaults and convert) and WP-56 (stage H validate): architecture R-7 overrides 01 J 39's RZ-CFG-005 row ('filterClass only for plugin') and 01 note 9. The registry materializes spec.filterClass on every Policy, so neither stage may reject a non-plugin Policy whose authored filterClass restates its registry class. registry.Registry.CheckFilterClass (internal/config/registry/policy.go:150-165) is the only filterClass rule. It reports RZ-CFG-005 for a differing value on a non-plugin type, or a non-class value on plugin. Call it once per Policy at stage H (WP-56) and add the source Location to its diagnostic, which carries Resource, Path and Message. Add no other filterClass check in defaults, convert or validate.

extra.WP-49:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 9 from WP-20] No SPI change is needed. WP-06 (committed) already defines the documented auth.Challenger in internal/filter/auth/auth.go:69-77, and *auth.Decider implements Challenge() (decider.go:63). The executor asserts an identical executor.Challenger on p.Filter (run.go:195) for the 401 RZ-AUTH-001 of Security rule 1. Note for WP-47, WP-48 and WP-49: the Filter value your Factory returns MUST have its own `Challenge() string` method. Get it by embedding *auth.Decider anonymously (promoted method) or by forwarding to it. A Decider held in a named field is invisible to the executor's type assertion, and the 401 then carries no WWW-Authenticate. Build the Decider with auth.NewAuth(m, challenge): auth.jwt uses auth.ChallengeJWT, auth.api-key uses auth.APIKeyChallenge(auth.APIKeyHeader(cfg.Header)), auth.basic uses auth.ChallengeBasic, and auth.mtls uses "" (no challenge, a documented deviation). Add a unit test per type asserting that p.Filter.(interface{ Challenge() string }) succeeds with the expected value.
- [CR 29 from WP-06] WP-70: give every snapshot compile its own filter.BuildEnv.Shared. It is a concurrency-safe, single-flight memo shared by all W workers of that compile and dropped afterwards. Build snapshot.Consumers and every BuildEnv.Consumers from one identity.CompileBundle(validated.Bundle).Map(), so the identity.Index from auth.AcquireIndex returns the same *expr.Consumer pointers the snapshot holds. On a failed or abandoned compile, Close (filter.Closer) every Filter already built so its index reference is released; otherwise a KeyIndex keeps its secret watches, or a later acquirer gets auth.ErrIndexClosed. WP-47/48/49 (auth.jwt, auth.api-key, auth.basic, auth.mtls): call auth.AcquireIndex(env) in Build, including when reusing env.Previous, because Consumers can change without the Policy changing. Each must implement auth.IndexHolder (`CredentialIndex() *identity.Index`, returning the held index) so the next compile carries the KeyIndex over (R-55), and call Index.Release() exactly once from Close.

- [CR 37 from WP-07] WP-53 (examples/quickstart, the examples/file-mode README) and WP-95 (Compose suite with bind-mounted secrets): create secret files with an explicit mode 0600 or 0644 (chmod or install -m), never relying on umask. - [Decision 2026-10-09, OQ-data-plane-18 (b)] Admin 404 and 405 problem documents carry codes: any path outside the admin table is 404 RZ-RT-020 ("No admin endpoint") and any other method on a known path is 405 RZ-RT-021 ("Method not allowed on admin endpoint"), both registered in internal/errcode with titles in internal/problem. Build them with internal/problem like every other admin error (never a bare net/http 404 or an empty code), set Allow on the 405, answer 404 and 405 only after adminauth admits the request (an unknown path without an admitted operator credential stays 401, internal/adminauth/adminauth.go:13-19), treat HEAD as another method (a ServeMux "GET /x" pattern also matches HEAD, and the admin table lists GET only), and test both on every admin path and method.
